speaker: Nemotron Ultra
text: IREN is a risk manager's nightmare: a 95.7% max drawdown, four consecutive quarters of deep operating losses, and a 2.83 beta that amplifies every Nasdaq wobble. The street's $40-91 targets assume a bitcoin-mining-to-AI-pivot that hasn't shown up in revenue yet — latest quarter still shrank 5% year-over-year. With $100 US budget, fractional shares remove the price barrier, but the 0.38% India delivery breakeven on Reliance via Zerodha (STT Rs 20 + exchange Rs 0.59 + SEBI Rs 0.02 + stamp Rs 1.5 + GST Rs 0.11 + DP Rs 15.93 = Rs 38.15 round-trip) means you need 0.38% just to scratch. IPO allotment on $10 is a lottery ticket — most US IPOs require $2,500+ minimums, and Indian IPOs need Rs 15,000 per lot. For the 10x goal, IREN's volatility could deliver it or zero you out; cash preserves optionality until a setup with positive expectancy appears.

text: TENB's Q3 showed revenue climbing 9.5% year-over-year to $276M and operating margin expanding to 6.1%, the best in five quarters — proof the platform shift is finally dropping to the bottom line. The street still has twelve holds against only eight buys, and the median target sits around $47, just 5% above today's $44.68 print, so upside is capped unless next quarter accelerates. Insiders have sold $7M worth in the last six months with zero buys, which rarely signals near-term confidence. For your $100 US sleeve, a fractional position is fine, but size it as a satellite bet, not a core holding, because the 10x math still demands names that can compound above 20% annually.
